scope: Add a post-redemption duplicate-identity check to the link-callback's `redeemed` branch. Today `runLinkCallbackExchange` treats every `redeemed` status as unconditional success (src/routes/auth/callback/run-link-callback.ts:79-113): it persists user/token and returns `ok:true`. Entu's own `conflict` flag cannot catch a user re-linking a provider they already have (verified against entu-api's `index.get.js` same-entity branch — see implementationNotes): the fresh self-invite placeholder gets `replaceInviteWithCredentials`-written with the SAME uid+provider as an already-bound entry, entu-api returns a clean `redeemed`-shaped body, and the person ends up with two identical `entu_user` array entries. The fix is entirely client-side: (1) snapshot the pre-mint linked set (uid+provider pairs) into the existing OAuth-state blob at mint time (src/routes/profile/+page.svelte's `handleLinkProvider`, threaded through `buildOAuthInitUrl`'s `OAuthState`), (2) after `redeemed`, re-read `entu_user` via the existing `listLinkedIdentities`, identify the newly-bound entry (its property `_id` is the mint's own placeholder `_id`, absent from the pre-mint snapshot), and check its uid+provider against the snapshot, (3) on a match, redirect through the SAME already-existing (currently dead-code) `link_error=already_linked` outcome the entu-side tripwire branch already produces (run-link-callback.ts:63-68) — no new UI/i18n path needed — and DELETE the duplicate `property/{id}` with the freshly-redeemed token, swallowing (logging only) a rights refusal, (4) on no match, unchanged success. Persistence (`setUser`/`setToken`/`hydrateAuth`/`hydrateCollectives`) should still run unconditionally per the issue's "do not fail the sign-in" rule — only the final redirect/outcome branches on the duplicate check.

implementationNotes:
Mechanism, confirmed by reading the code (not inferred):

1. MINT SITE / SNAPSHOT: `handleLinkProvider` (profile/+page.svelte:534-572) has `linkedIdentities` (LinkedIdentity[] with `_id,uid,provider,email`) already loaded in component state before it calls `mintSelfLinkInvite` then `buildOAuthInitUrl`. The snapshot of uid+provider pairs must be captured HERE and threaded as a new field on `OAuthInitArgs`/`OAuthState` (state.ts:15-35, build-oauth-init-url.ts:5-25), following the EXACT existing pattern `invite`/`linkPersonId` already use — persisted to `localStorage[OAUTH_STATE_KEY]` (state.ts:13, written at build-oauth-init-url.ts:48). This does NOT touch Path C's governed keys (`token`/`accounts`/`user`, storage.ts) — the OAuth-state blob is a separate, already-precedented CSRF/handoff carrier, single-use-consumed at run-callback-exchange.ts:29-30. No Path C violation.

2. MINT MECHANICS (verified in src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:371-461, `mintSelfLinkInvite`): each click sweeps any stale unredeemed placeholder first, then POSTs `entity/{personId}` with `[{type:'entu_user', string: INVITE_MINT_TRIGGER}]` — Entu POST APPENDS (project convention), so this always creates a FRESH `entu_user` property value with a NEW `_id`. entu-api's `replaceInviteWithCredentials` (index.get.js:284-291 @7853ada) later mutates THAT SAME `_id` in place (`_id: invitePropId`) — it never creates a second id. So the newly-bound identity's property `_id`, post-redemption, is deterministically the SAME `_id` the mint call itself returned (mintBody.properties[].invite match, inviteData.ts:452-459) — it is NOT necessary to diff two re-read lists by set-difference; the exact target `_id` can be threaded through state at mint time instead, then looked up directly in the post-redemption re-read. This is simpler/more robust than the issue's literal "snapshot the whole set, diff after" framing, though both arrive at the same answer; worth flagging to whoever writes RED as a possible simplification.

3. WHY ENTU'S OWN `conflict` FLAG CANNOT CATCH THIS (traced exactly through index.get.js @7853ada, unchanged in kind on origin/main): the top-level `conflict:'invite'` is set ONLY on the "different entity" branch (line 226-229, `existingEntry.user._id !== inviteData.entityId`). Re-linking an ALREADY-OWN identity hits the sibling `else if (existingEntry.user._id === inviteData.entityId)` branch (line 225, "clean up orphaned invite property") — no conflict flag, `replaceInviteWithCredentials` still runs, and mvox's `exchangeSessionWithInvite` (redeem.ts) sees a normal accounts-entry match against `expectedEntityId` and classifies it `status:'redeemed'`, `personId: linkPersonId` — INDISTINGUISHABLE at the wire level from a legitimate new link. Client-side re-read+diff is not a design nicety, it's the only way to detect this given the current (and 7853ada) exchange contract.

4. WHOSE TOKEN FOR THE POST-REDEMPTION RE-READ + DELETE: use `result.token` (the just-redeemed, account-scoped-to-`invite.db` JWT), not `existingToken` — it's guaranteed valid for `invite.db`+`linkPersonId` regardless of whether a broader pre-existing session token exists (mirrors how the existing persist block already treats `result.token` as authoritative for this db). `listLinkedIdentities(cfg, linkPersonId, fetch)` (linkedIdentities.ts:46-80) is the exact existing reusable function for the re-read; the DELETE call should follow the established `entuFetch(cfg.db, \`property/${id}\`, cfg.token, {method:'DELETE'}, fetchImpl)` shape used identically in replaceProperty.ts:71, repertoireActions.ts:126/162/249, seasonManage.ts:178/218, sectionActions.ts:267/333/480/545, roleManagement.ts:261/299, and inviteData.ts's own stale-placeholder sweep (inviteData.ts:401-415) — NOT `DELETE /entity/{id}` (per project's own documented entity-vs-property split, MEMORY.md `project_entu_wire_shape_entity_vs_property`).

5. RIGHTS REFUSAL SHAPE: `entuFetch` (src/lib/entu/request.ts:111-132) intercepts ONLY HTTP 401 (auth-expiry, routed to the centralized `handleAuthExpired401()` / install-401-recovery.ts flow) — every other status, including a rights-refusal, passes through untouched as a plain Response for the caller to inspect. inviteData.ts's own self-_editor mint gate observes this refusal as a 403 (`self-link mint refused: HTTP 403`, inviteData.ts:436-439) on a DIFFERENT endpoint (entity POST) — the analogous property DELETE refusal has NOT been directly observed in this codebase (no test/comment pins its exact status for `property/{id}` DELETE specifically) and should be treated as `[unverified]` until probed; code should check `!delRes.ok` generically (any non-2xx) rather than special-casing 403, matching the issue's "log it ... do not fail the sign-in" instruction and avoiding a RED-time assumption about the exact code. This is a genuinely open, checkable-but-unchecked-here fact — safe to leave generic in the implementation.

6. OUTCOME REUSE: the `already_linked` redirect/message path ALREADY EXISTS end-to-end and is currently dead code — `run-link-callback.ts:63-68` (the entu-side same-person-conflict tripwire, `error:'link_already_linked'`, `redirectTo:'/profile?link_error=already_linked'`) and the profile page's `?link_error=` consumer (added per bentham.md #193 round-1 note) both already render `profile_link_error_already_linked` (verified present, byte-identical intent, in all four locales: messages/en.json:146 'That sign-in is already linked to your account.', et.json:146, lv.json:146, uk.json:146). Sub-change B's new duplicate-detected branch can reuse this EXACT outcome shape rather than inventing a new error/redirect key — no new i18n work is needed for this sub-change specifically.

7. RIGHTS ON THE PERSON ENTITY: confirmed both mvox's own invite-mint path (inviteData.ts:252-271, POST `[{type:'_editor', reference: personId}]`) and entu-api's native auto-create (`createUserForAccount`, index.get.js:330 @7853ada / same at origin/main) grant self-`_editor` at person-creation time — this is the rights basis the existing profile name/email self-save already exercises (profileData.ts:282-329, same cfg.token/entuFetch pattern) and that the new duplicate-DELETE would rely on. Whether every already-seeded real ('crede') person in the live db actually carries this grant is NOT verified here (scripts/migrations/seed-178-crede-members-2026-08-27.ts only sets `_owner` on a MEMBER entity, not self-`_editor` on the person; person-entity creation itself for those members happens elsewhere/earlier and was not traced) — flagged `[unverified]`, but low-risk: the existing `mintSelfLinkInvite` 403 gate (missing-self-editor) already fires BEFORE the OAuth round-trip even starts for any such person, and the issue's own spec already prescribes graceful log-and-continue for a delete-side rights refusal.

implementationNotes:
**Mechanism, independently verified against entu-api source (clone 7853ada AND origin/main tip f86c907, 2026-08-19 — logic unchanged across that range, confirmed by diff):** `GET/auth?account=<db>&invite=<token>` resolves `existingEntry` by matching the JUST-authenticated OAuth session's `uid`+`provider` against ALL persons in the target db (index.get.js:157-164). Three branches on that lookup vs. the invite's target entity (`inviteData.entityId`, i.e. `linkPersonId`): (a) no match → normal accept, mints the new identity onto the invite's placeholder (:217-224, this is the everyday "second Google account" case); (b) match IS the same person (`existingEntry.user._id === inviteData.entityId`, :225-229) → **same-identity re-link**: `replaceInviteWithCredentials` still runs, converting the self-mint's placeholder `entu_user` entry (a distinct array entry with its own `_id`, created moments earlier by `mintSelfLinkInvite` in inviteData.ts) into a full credentials entry with the SAME uid/provider/email as the pre-existing entry — this is the duplicate, and `inviteConflict` is NEVER set for this branch, so the exchange returns clean `redeemed`; (c) match is a DIFFERENT person → `inviteConflict = true`, surfaced as `body.conflict === 'invite'`.

mvox's own `redeem.ts` classifies `body.conflict === 'invite'` as `status: 'conflict'`, and there's already a test (`run-link-callback.spec.ts:192-210`, "a SAME-person conflict is classified as already_linked") for `conflict` + `existingPersonId === linkPersonId` — but per the entu-api trace above, entu-api's `inviteConflict` flag is **only ever set for the different-person branch**; the same-person case never reaches `conflict` status at all. This existing test therefore covers an input shape that is (per current entu-api source) unreachable in practice — it is defensive/tripwire coverage, not a test of the actual same-identity path. The actual same-identity duplicate goes through `status: 'redeemed'` silently, exactly as #219's body claims. This is the single most important fact to hand to RED: **the new same-identity detection cannot key off `result.status === 'conflict'`; it must compare the redeemed identity against a pre-mint snapshot, because entu-api gives no signal.**

Concrete mechanism for the snapshot/compare (issue's steps 1-3, none of it exists today): (1) at click time in `+page.svelte`, before calling `mintSelfLinkInvite`, the already-loaded `linkedIdentities` (from `listLinkedIdentities`) gives the pre-mint set; that set's `{_id, uid, provider}` triples (not just uid+provider — the `_id`s are needed so the post-redemption diff can target a DELETE, since `DELETE /property/{id}` needs a property id, not a uid+provider pair) must ride through the OAuth round trip. The only carrier is `OAuthState` (verified: currently has no such field — this is a genuinely new, additive field, `intent:'link'`-only, low blast radius). (2) After `redeemed`, in `run-link-callback.ts`, re-read `listLinkedIdentities({db: state.invite.db, token: <post-redemption token>}, state.linkPersonId)` — MUST use `state.invite.db`/`state.linkPersonId`, never `$selectedCollectiveStore` (a live reactive store the headless callback module does not and should not import), so the check can never touch the wrong db even if the user switched collectives mid-round-trip in another tab. (3) Diff by `uid`+`provider`: any pair whose post-read `_id` set is a superset of its pre-mint `_id` set (i.e., a new `_id` appeared for an already-occupied uid+provider pair) is the duplicate; the new `_id` (present post, absent pre) is what to `DELETE /property/{id}` — this is the exact existing pattern already used three lines away in the SAME file's sibling module, `inviteData.ts:404` (`entuFetch(cfg.db, \`property/${stale._id}\`, cfg.token, {method:'DELETE'}, fetchImpl)`), so GREEN has a direct precedent to copy, not a new wire shape to invent.

**Rights (self-_editor), resolved, not merely flagged**: `mintSelfLinkInvite` itself requires the caller to already hold self-`_editor` on their own person (a 403 there is the existing `missing-self-editor` SelfLinkMintError, thrown BEFORE the OAuth redirect even happens). Therefore, by the time execution reaches the post-redemption duplicate-check/delete step, self-`_editor` is already proven present (the mint could not have succeeded otherwise) — the delete this issue plans can only fail on rights in the rare case of a mid-flight revocation between mint and return, not as a routine gap. Separately, `inviteData.ts` (the ADMIN-invite mint path, a different function in the same file) makes granting self-`_editor` a hard, verified precondition of sending any invite at all (lines 252-268: grant failure aborts the whole invite-create loudly) — so invite-redeemed persons created via mvox's current invite flow are guaranteed to have it; Entu's native `createUserForAccount` grants it automatically for auto-provisioned persons (verified at entu-api :330-331 / :289-290 depending on commit). The only realistic rights-gap population is legacy/pre-refactor persons or ad-hoc migration-script-created persons that bypass both paths (2 of 35 seed scripts create person-shaped entities without an `_editor` grant, grep-verified) — a pre-existing condition, not introduced by #219.
